quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Your position does not matter.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when behind a car. This position makes you visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is not flat.
Brake using the good tire and steer toward the road's edge.
Loosen your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the good tire and steer toward the road's edge.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Brake gradually using only the good tire. As you slow down, move toward the edge of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It works just as well as a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
All motorcycles are required to have one.
You should only use it on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace the protection of goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not fully protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop, in all situations.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to riding during the day, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower.
Keep more distance from other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.
Ride closely behind other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase the distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles to avoid crashes. Use headlights ahead to see the road. Stay flexible with your lane position at night.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They happen at night.
They involve riders with little experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with little experience.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen with riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer roads to ride on.

questions.explanation: Make yourself visible to reduce crash risk. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on your motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It damages the engine and should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear creates a braking effect. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handlebar.
On the right handlebar.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handlebar of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When using a sidecar to carry a load, what should you do?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load in the seat without securing it.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Loads in a sidecar must be secured so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Put the weight toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the front from tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. These signs tell drivers what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: What can help you avoid accidents?

options.text: Blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Signal your turns and lane changes. Use your brake light and position yourself clearly. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds for hazards and be ready to react.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: Both should lean together at the same angle.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: The motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle during normal turns. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no traffic is in your way.

questions.question: How should you usually handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move to the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make the situation more dangerous.
